lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: the paper (Sep 2023) postdates both data its SME comparison uses -- the Eot-Wash 38.6 um edge (2020) and the ~1e-21 trapped-ion electron bound (Dreissen 2022) -- and its formula's only other input is G (CODATA value unchanged 2018 -> 2022). No datum that has moved since was found, and none could move the conclusion: at the Eot-Wash edge the prediction is 1.57e42 below the bound, and the most any unread O(1) factor (I_grav at b^2 = 1, an alpha = 2 edge at 20-30 um, 3% in Mbar4) moves it is < 1 order (computed). Evidence AGAINST 'lacked data' is therefore strong for the numerical null at r = 38.6 um. What IS missing is not data but a reading: the source itself could not be opened here, so eq. 77's limit, its b^2 domain and the identity of mu are unverified, and the tree's own inequality direction over r is a computed discrepancy in its use, not a defect of the external result.
grade_evidence: The external result (eqs. 76-77) could not be READ at source this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted on 4 calls; arxiv/inspire/APS/Springer/Semantic Scholar refused by the egress proxy), and I_gravity's zeta(3)/4 limit is a loop integral whose definition is not available, so it is neither STANDS nor WRONG. What was checked: the tree's arithmetic of the RESTATED eq. 76 reproduces exactly (6.372236e-64, 42.196 orders; tensor factor 3 beta^2/4 proved in sympy; independent of higgs.py). Recorded discrepancies in the tree's USE, none a refutation of the source: (i) 'at the maximal r ... |c| <= 6.37e-64' has the wrong direction over r (|c| ~ 1/r^2; Eot-Wash bounds r above, so 6.37e-64 is the infimum at beta = 1; the SME bound bites at r <= 3.08e-26 m); (ii) the mu r -> 0 hypothesis is asserted, never evaluated (mu r ~ 1e8 IF mu = m_e); (iii) the zeta(3)/4 value may be a small-b^2 limit applied at b^2 = 1; (iv) beta = 1 is attained on neither graviton branch (conservative). The 42-orders null at the Eot-Wash edge is robust to every checkable move (< 1 order).
what_would_change_the_grade: READING arXiv:2309.05759 eqs. 74-77, 84 and Fig. 7 at source: if eq. 77's -zeta(3)/4 is stated for all b^2 (or I(1) is within O(1) of it), mu is shown not to be the external fermion mass/momentum (or the mu r >> 1 regime is shown to only shrink |I|), and eq. 76 matches the restatement, the result grades STANDS for the formula, with the tree's use NARROWED by the r-direction discrepancy (the null holds at r = 38.6 um, not over r <= 38.6 um). If the source's limit holds only at b^2 -> 0 or mu r -> 0 with mu = m_e, the tree's use at beta = 1, r = 38.6 um is NARROWED (outside the stated hypotheses) though the numerical null would survive unless |I| grew by ~1e42. A re-computation of the winding-loop integral showing a different coefficient would be needed for WRONG.
